page: Microsoft Azure E8s_v3 is an ESv3-family virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this x86_64 architecture server features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a 131 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU resources are included.

Benchmark data indicates moderate memory subsystem performance alongside weaker computational throughput. The server achieves average ratings in Passmark memory scores, database operations, and memory bandwidth, with read-only large block bandwidth reaching 42.29 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 30.27 GB/sec. However, CPU-heavy tasks show limitations, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core performance falling into the bottom 25 percent. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores are weak, though software compilation with Clang and ray tracing tests reach average tiers.

The primary tradeoff of the E8s_v3 is its high memory capacity relative to its modest processing speeds. While database operations and memory-bound tasks perform at average levels, compute-intensive workloads like text processing, image processing, and large-scale LLM inference are constrained by the CPU. Consequently, this server is best suited for memory-optimized workloads that do not require high-frequency compute, such as relational databases, caching layers, and moderate-scale enterprise applications.
